headline: Fee income drives profit growth, cash dips on payouts
summary_short: Revenue rose 24.0% y/y to $1,338M and net income climbed 15.6% y/y to $586M ($0.38 diluted EPS), as Fee-Related Earnings grew 11% to $772M and Distributable Earnings rose 7% to $702M; cash fell 34.0% q/q to $1,045M after $376M of buybacks and roughly $809M of dividend distributions.
summary_long: Revenue grew 24% y/y to $1,338M on higher base management fees (+7%), incentive distributions (+11%), and transaction fees, pushing Fee Revenues to $1,426M. Fee-Related Earnings rose 11% to $772M as fee growth outpaced an 8% rise in direct costs from headcount growth. Distributable Earnings increased 7% to $702M, with higher Fee-Related Earnings partly offset by higher interest expense and cash taxes. Net income rose 15.6% y/y to $586M ($0.38 diluted EPS) despite a 46% jump in total expenses, driven by higher share-based and carried-interest compensation. Total Fee-Bearing Capital grew 2% q/q to $613.8B. BAM paid a $0.5025/share dividend and repurchased $376M of stock in the quarter, pulling cash down to $1,045M. No forward guidance was given in the filing.

Revenue grew $257M on higher fee income while total expenses grew $231M on higher share-based and carried-interest compensation; the larger dollar increase in revenue drove income higher despite faster expense growth.

Higher pretax income was partly offset by a $35M rise in income tax expense, which the filing attributes to higher taxable income compared to the prior period.

The filing attributes the $224M increase to net dispositions from consolidated funds, higher cash generated from fee revenues, and net changes in working capital.
Cash fell $538M q/q on $376M of share repurchases and roughly $809M of dividend distributions, partly offset by $400M of new related-party deposits.
Equity fell $326M q/q as treasury stock grew $390M from buybacks and retained deficit widened $196M, partly offset by a $105M rise in non-controlling interests.
Broad fee growth (Fee Revenues +10% to $1,426M) lifted Fee-Related Earnings 11% and Distributable Earnings 7%, while cash fell on quarterly dividends and buybacks; no forward guidance was given.
